ref_clues.ref_content: This fatal alert is triggered upon detecting a fatal fault inside the AES unit. Examples for such faults include i) storage errors in the shadowed Control Register, ii) any internal FSM entering an invalid state, iii) any sparsely encoded signal taking on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus. The AES unit cannot recover from such an error and needs to be reset.

If any countermeasure (shadow register mismatch, sparse encoding fault, multi-rail control logic fault, hardened round counter fault) detects a fault, a fatal alert is triggered. Internal FSMs go to a terminal error state, the AES unit ceases to release data and locks up until a system reset. This condition is reported in STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.

ref_clues.ref_content: Auxiliary Control Register. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). FORCE_MASKS (bit 1): Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.

ref_clues.ref_content: Covers that KEY, IV, DATA registers can be written in random order and interleaved, and that an operation is triggered. Data out can be read in random order.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). The AES unit indicates output data availability via a status register. A back-pressure mechanism stalls the AES unit when finishing a block but previous output data not yet read by the processor; it hangs, does not drop data, and continues only after the previous output registers are read (any order, each read at least once). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit never stalls and overwrites previous output data regardless of read status.
The initial key and control register can only be updated by the processor when the AES unit is idle.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.

If any countermeasure (shadow register mismatch, sparse encoding fault, multi-rail control logic fault, hardened round counter fault) detects a fault, a fatal alert is triggered. Internal FSMs go to a terminal error state, the AES unit ceases to release data and locks up until a system reset. This condition is reported in STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT.

Covers that all valid settings for operation (encode/decode/illegal), mode (all modes + illegal/aes_none), key_len (128/192/256 + illegal), sideload, prng_reseed_rate (all + illegal), and manual operation have been tested, including illegal values. All valid combinations of these will be crossed.

Control Register. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode. A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message. Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards. Fields: OPERATION (bits 1:0): 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01). MODE (bits 7:2): 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b10_0000). KEY_LEN (bits 10:8): 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100). SIDELOAD (bit 11): Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers. PRNG_RESEED_RATE (bits 14:12): 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal PRNG used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001). MANUAL_OPERATION (bit 15): Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode, the AES unit automatically starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode, the AES unit only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger, and overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.

Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
The cipher core FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by CIPHER.FSM.SPARSE, CIPHER.FSM.REDUN, CIPHER.CTR.REDUN, CTRL.SPARSE as well as MAIN.FSM.LOCAL_ESC.

Verify the countermeasure(s) CTRL.SPARSE. It is ensured that upon randomly forcing the value of any of these critical control signals to an invalid encoding, the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.

The AES unit supports both encryption and decryption for AES-128/192/256 in ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR modes using a single, shared data path. That is, it can either do encryption or decryption but not both at the same time.

ref_clues.ref_content: Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. While executing any of the triggered operations, the AES unit will set the IDLE bit in the Status Register to zero. The processor must check the Status Register before triggering further actions. For example, writes to Initial Key and IV Registers are ignored while the AES unit is busy. Writes to the Input Data Registers are not ignored but the data will be cleared if a KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR operation is pending. Fields: START (bit 0): Keep AES unit paused (0) or trigger the encryption/decryption of one data block (1). This trigger is cleared to 0 if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 or if MODE=AES_NONE. KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR (bit 1): Keep current values in Initial Key, internal Full Key and Decryption Key registers, IV registers and Input Data registers (0) or clear all those registers with pseudo-random data (1). DATA_OUT_CLEAR (bit 2): Keep current values in Output Data registers (0) or clear those registers with pseudo-random data (1). PRNG_RESEED (bit 3): Keep continuing with the current states of the internal pseudo-random number generators used for register clearing and masking (0) or perform a reseed of the internal states from the connected entropy source (1). If the KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED bit in the Auxiliary Control Register is set to one, this trigger will automatically get set after providing a new initial key.

Covers that start initiates an operation in manual mode but not when not in manual mode. A write to key_iv_data_in/data_out_clear clears the data from the register. Additionally, transitioning from automatic to manual mode prevents triggering a start without re-configuring (writing to CTRL).

Cover that the DUT self clearing is working correctly. After reset, manually writing trigger.start and polling status.idle must show DUT stays idle; output registers should contain random data (output cleared).

ref_clues.ref_content: Auxiliary Control Register. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). FORCE_MASKS (bit 1): Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.

If any countermeasure (shadow register mismatch, sparse encoding fault, multi-rail control logic fault, hardened round counter fault) detects a fault, a fatal alert is triggered. Internal FSMs go to a terminal error state, the AES unit ceases to release data and locks up until a system reset. This condition is reported in STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. ref_clues.ref_content: Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

In CTR mode, the counter module iteratively increments the 128-bit counter value stored in the IV register using a 16-bit counter, requiring 8 clock cycles per increment. The counter value is used in the first round only, so the overall throughput is not affected given the 12/14/16-cycle block latency.

ref_clues.ref_content: Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. While executing any of the triggered operations, the AES unit will set the IDLE bit in the Status Register to zero. The processor must check the Status Register before triggering further actions. For example, writes to Initial Key and IV Registers are ignored while the AES unit is busy. Writes to the Input Data Registers are not ignored but the data will be cleared if a KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR operation is pending. Fields: START (bit 0): Keep AES unit paused (0) or trigger the encryption/decryption of one data block (1). This trigger is cleared to 0 if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 or if MODE=AES_NONE. KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR (bit 1): Keep current values in Initial Key, internal Full Key and Decryption Key registers, IV registers and Input Data registers (0) or clear all those registers with pseudo-random data (1). DATA_OUT_CLEAR (bit 2): Keep current values in Output Data registers (0) or clear those registers with pseudo-random data (1). PRNG_RESEED (bit 3): Keep continuing with the current states of the internal pseudo-random number generators used for register clearing and masking (0) or perform a reseed of the internal states from the connected entropy source (1). If the KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED bit in the Auxiliary Control Register is set to one, this trigger will automatically get set after providing a new initial key.

ref_clues.ref_content: When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.

In CTR mode, the counter module iteratively increments the 128-bit counter value stored in the IV register using a 16-bit counter, requiring 8 clock cycles per increment. The counter value is used in the first round only, so the overall throughput is not affected given the 12/14/16-cycle block latency.
The DOM S-Box has a latency of 5 clock cycles. All other S-Box implementations (Masked Canright, unmasked Canright, LUT) are fully combinational with one S-Box evaluation per clock cycle.

ref_clues.ref_content: Auxiliary Control Register. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). FORCE_MASKS (bit 1): Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

In automatic mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=0 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption when the previous operation finished, new input data is available, all input registers written at least once (any order), and in CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR modes the IV is ready (all IV registers written at least once or none since last update; partially updated IV will not start). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1), encryption/decryption starts only when the START bit in TRIGGER is set to 1, and START is automatically cleared to 0 once the next operation starts.

Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

ref_clues.ref_content: When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.

Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ref_clues.ref_content: Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. While executing any of the triggered operations, the AES unit will set the IDLE bit in the Status Register to zero. The processor must check the Status Register before triggering further actions. For example, writes to Initial Key and IV Registers are ignored while the AES unit is busy. Writes to the Input Data Registers are not ignored but the data will be cleared if a KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR operation is pending. Fields: START (bit 0): Keep AES unit paused (0) or trigger the encryption/decryption of one data block (1). This trigger is cleared to 0 if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 or if MODE=AES_NONE. KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR (bit 1): Keep current values in Initial Key, internal Full Key and Decryption Key registers, IV registers and Input Data registers (0) or clear all those registers with pseudo-random data (1). DATA_OUT_CLEAR (bit 2): Keep current values in Output Data registers (0) or clear those registers with pseudo-random data (1). PRNG_RESEED (bit 3): Keep continuing with the current states of the internal pseudo-random number generators used for register clearing and masking (0) or perform a reseed of the internal states from the connected entropy source (1). If the KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED bit in the Auxiliary Control Register is set to one, this trigger will automatically get set after providing a new initial key.

Covers that start initiates an operation in manual mode but not when not in manual mode. A write to key_iv_data_in/data_out_clear clears the data from the register. Additionally, transitioning from automatic to manual mode prevents triggering a start without re-configuring (writing to CTRL).

If MANUAL_OPERATION=0, the AES unit is stalled when the previous output data has not yet been read and is about to be overwritten. Each register has to be read at least once. The order in which the registers are read does not matter. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ref_clues.ref_content: Covers that KEY, IV, DATA registers can be written in random order and interleaved, and that an operation is triggered. Data out can be read in random order.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.

Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

In automatic mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=0 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption when the previous operation finished, new input data is available, all input registers written at least once (any order), and in CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR modes the IV is ready (all IV registers written at least once or none since last update; partially updated IV will not start). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1), encryption/decryption starts only when the START bit in TRIGGER is set to 1, and START is automatically cleared to 0 once the next operation starts.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). ref_clues.ref_content: Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

The processor can only update the IV registers when the AES unit is idle. In CBC or CTR mode, when the AES unit is busy, it updates the IV registers itself. The IV registers are updated with output data (CBC encryption) or previous input data (CBC decryption); in CFB mode with output data; in OFB mode with the output of the final cipher round before XORing with previous input data.

In automatic mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=0 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption when the previous operation finished, new input data is available, all input registers written at least once (any order), and in CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR modes the IV is ready (all IV registers written at least once or none since last update; partially updated IV will not start). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1), encryption/decryption starts only when the START bit in TRIGGER is set to 1, and START is automatically cleared to 0 once the next operation starts.

In CTR mode, the counter module iteratively increments the 128-bit counter value stored in the IV register using a 16-bit counter, requiring 8 clock cycles per increment. The counter value is used in the first round only, so the overall throughput is not affected given the 12/14/16-cycle block latency.

The AES unit supports both encryption and decryption for AES-128/192/256 in ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR modes using a single, shared data path. That is, it can either do encryption or decryption but not both at the same time.

ref_clues.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

In CTR mode, the counter module iteratively increments the 128-bit counter value stored in the IV register using a 16-bit counter, requiring 8 clock cycles per increment. The counter value is used in the first round only, so the overall throughput is not affected given the 12/14/16-cycle block latency.

ref_clues.ref_content: If any countermeasure (shadow register mismatch, sparse encoding fault, multi-rail control logic fault, hardened round counter fault) detects a fault, a fatal alert is triggered. Internal FSMs go to a terminal error state, the AES unit ceases to release data and locks up until a system reset. This condition is reported in STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT.

Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

The main control register (CTRL_SHADOWED) is shadowed: software performs two write operations to update, and a shadow copy is constantly compared with the actual register. If a mismatch occurs, a fatal alert is triggered.

ref_clues.ref_content: Control Register. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode. A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message. Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards. Fields: OPERATION (bits 1:0): 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01). MODE (bits 7:2): 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b10_0000). KEY_LEN (bits 10:8): 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100). SIDELOAD (bit 11): Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers. PRNG_RESEED_RATE (bits 14:12): 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal PRNG used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001). MANUAL_OPERATION (bit 15): Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode, the AES unit automatically starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode, the AES unit only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger, and overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.

Covers that all valid settings for operation (encode/decode/illegal), mode (all modes + illegal/aes_none), key_len (128/192/256 + illegal), sideload, prng_reseed_rate (all + illegal), and manual operation have been tested, including illegal values. All valid combinations of these will be crossed.

Output Data Register. Holds the output data produced by the AES unit during the last encryption/decryption operation. If MANUAL_OPERATION=0, the AES unit is stalled when the previous output data has not yet been read and is about to be overwritten. Each register has to be read at least once. The order in which the registers are read does not matter. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

The AES unit indicates output data availability via a status register. A back-pressure mechanism stalls the AES unit when finishing a block but previous output data not yet read by the processor; it hangs, does not drop data, and continues only after the previous output registers are read (any order, each read at least once). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit never stalls and overwrites previous output data regardless of read status.

ref_clues.ref_content: Control Register. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode. A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message. Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards. Fields: OPERATION (bits 1:0): 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01). MODE (bits 7:2): 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b10_0000). KEY_LEN (bits 10:8): 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100). SIDELOAD (bit 11): Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers. PRNG_RESEED_RATE (bits 14:12): 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal PRNG used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001). MANUAL_OPERATION (bit 15): Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode, the AES unit automatically starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode, the AES unit only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger, and overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.

ref_clues.ref_content: The cipher core FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by CIPHER.FSM.SPARSE, CIPHER.FSM.REDUN, CIPHER.CTR.REDUN, CTRL.SPARSE as well as MAIN.FSM.LOCAL_ESC.

This fatal alert is triggered upon detecting a fatal fault inside the AES unit. Examples for such faults include i) storage errors in the shadowed Control Register, ii) any internal FSM entering an invalid state, iii) any sparsely encoded signal taking on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus. The AES unit cannot recover from such an error and needs to be reset.

Verify the countermeasure(s) CIPHER.FSM.REDUN. It is ensured that upon randomly forcing the state, inputs or outputs of any of the independent, redundant logic rails of the cipher core FSM to both valid and invalid encodings, the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.

Verify the countermeasure(s) MAIN.FSM.REDUN. It is ensured that upon randomly forcing the state, inputs or outputs of any of the independent, redundant logic rails of the main FSM to both valid and invalid encodings, the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.

The masking PRNG is automatically reseeded with fresh entropy from EDN 1) whenever a new key is provided (if CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED.KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED is enabled) and 2) based on a block counter configured via CTRL_SHADOWED.PRNG_RESEED_RATE. Software can also manually initiate a reseed via TRIGGER.PRNG_RESEED.

ref_clues.ref_content: Auxiliary Control Register. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). FORCE_MASKS (bit 1): Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.

ref_clues.ref_content: The AES unit indicates output data availability via a status register. A back-pressure mechanism stalls the AES unit when finishing a block but previous output data not yet read by the processor; it hangs, does not drop data, and continues only after the previous output registers are read (any order, each read at least once). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit never stalls and overwrites previous output data regardless of read status.

Control Register. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode. A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message. Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards. Fields: OPERATION (bits 1:0): 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01). MODE (bits 7:2): 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b10_0000). KEY_LEN (bits 10:8): 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100). SIDELOAD (bit 11): Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers. PRNG_RESEED_RATE (bits 14:12): 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal PRNG used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001). MANUAL_OPERATION (bit 15): Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode, the AES unit automatically starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode, the AES unit only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger, and overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.
